Squash VR Trainer

WebXR · solo practice

Squash VR Trainer

clavelseb.github.io/squashvr

A regulation 9.75 × 6.40 m court and a ball that behaves like a warm double‑yellow. Drill drives, boasts, drops, nicks and returns of serve without leaving your spot.

Targets are worked out for each feed from where you will take the ball. Volley, loose-ball and boast-feed drills show a nick target on the front wall. Boast practice feeds deep into the back corner and shows a target on the side wall. Drive practice feeds down your wall to the back of the service box: the straight-drive target shows where to aim at your usual pace, and each drive is scored on length (a touch long beats short), how close it stays to the side wall all the way back, and touching the side wall late or not at all. Pace is shown but not scored. Each solo drill can be set to crosscourt nick, straight nick, boast, straight drive, straight drop, straight kill, crosscourt drive, crosscourt length, straight lob, crosscourt lob or no target.

The four main drills each run a sequence of blocks, the first two off the volley feed. The Nick shot drill (320 shots) gives each of the four nicks 10 shots off the normal feed, 10 off a slightly wider crosscourt feed, 10 slightly behind you, 10 further behind, 20 faster and 20 even faster; every shot scores 3 points for a nick or anything within 10 cm of it, 2 within 30 cm and 1 within 70 cm (all set in the menu). The Straight length drill (160 shots) uses the same feeds on each side for straight drives, rated as in drive practice: 3 points for a drive of 85 or more, 2 for 70, 1 for 50. The Front court drill (120 shots) feeds a straight drop from the back corner on your side, which you take low in the front court and answer six ways, 10 of each on the backhand and then the forehand: counter drop, straight drive, crosscourt drive (hard and low), straight lob, crosscourt lob and crosscourt nick. Each has its target on the front wall; drops, crosscourt drives and lobs are rated on where the ball goes (a drop on how short, low and tight it is, a crosscourt drive on length, width and height on the front wall, a lob on its height over the T line, its length and how close to the side wall it lands), with the same 3, 2 and 1 points. The Back court drill (160 shots) feeds straight drives from the T (or beside it, near the side wall), and you play from the back, eight exercises of 10, all on the backhand and then all on the forehand: a straight drive; the same off the back wall (an overhit feed that you let come out); a crosscourt length (to die in the far back corner, touching the side wall behind the service box or not at all); boasts off a deep drive that sits up in the corner; a straight drop; the same off the back wall; a straight kill off a loose, short length (low and hard, to die before the service box); and a crosscourt lob off a hard, low length. The feeds are identical unless you turn on small variation, and the blocks can be edited (up to 30). The menu opens on the main drills, with the history under them: every drill played to the end, 10 to a page, with the score, the average speed of your shots, your back-to-the-T and watching-the-ball scores and the breakdown by shot and by kind of feed. The solo drills, the Custom sequence (a sequence of your own), the ball and the other options are on the Solo & options tab.

Five boxes on the front wall follow your play: the drill (block, shot, points), the speed of your last shot, the last shot (its result, the points it earned and the details), back to the T, and a debug box (refresh rate and frame time) when Show: FPS is on. The speed, last-shot and back-to-the-T boxes keep the two shots before the last one, smaller, to compare.

The voice. In a main drill or a custom sequence a voice reads out each block as it starts (the first ball waits for it), each shot's result with its points (“Too loose. One point.”), and at the end of a block what to work on: “Make more effort to go back to the T!” if you covered less than half the way back on average, “Make more effort to watch the ball!” if you watched it less than 50 %. Racquet & settings sets it to blocks and every shot, blocks only, or off. The phrases are a recording that comes with the page, since the headset's browser has no speech of its own.

Back to the T. After each shot in a drill, a ring on the floor shows where to go back to: red, then yellow, then green as you get there, and the box on the wall says Go back, Closer or Excellent. You are rated on how much of the way you covered before the next ball leaves (all the way 100 %, staying where you hit 0 %), and the drill ends with your back-to-the-T score, kept in the history. By default the ring is the T itself in the main drills (1.2 m from the hitting spot) and a metre towards it in the drills played from further back; Solo & options sets it to up to 0.5 m, always the T, or off. In free play the box counts the shots of your rally.

Watching the ball. The drills feed the ball from behind you, so you should be looking back at the feeder as it leaves. Each feed is rated from how far your head is turned: 0 % facing the front wall, 100 % turned to where the ball comes from. Nothing is shown shot by shot; the drill's result gives the percentage, and it is kept in the history.

Fitting the court to your room. With the menu open the game is paused and the stick still moves you, so you can slide the court to where your room has space in the middle of a drill; Hitting spot here (Solo & options) puts the drill's hitting spot under your feet. Where the headset's browser gives its play area, its outline is drawn on the floor while the menu is open (or always).

Ball & racquet physics

Ball
24 g, 40 mm hollow shell, drag + Magnus lift
Bounce
Fitted to published drop and wall tests: 27 % rebound from 254 cm at 45 °C (the WSF test), fading as you hit harder: about 0.50 at 36 km/h, 0.32 at 105 km/h. Always warm by default (50 °C; or 40 or 45 °C), or start cold and warm it up
Contact
Soft contact, ~5 ms on the strings, grip on every wall and the floor. By default the ball is rigid and keeps no spin, so every bounce comes off as if it were not spinning and a boast's front-wall bounce is neutral. The Ball physics tab brings spin back (Bounce spin, Racquet spin) or makes the ball a soft shell that trades less spin with a wall (Rigid ball off)
Hit assist
The swing and the ball's path are traced through each frame; a ball that would clip the frame or just miss the head is put on the strings (off, 3, 6 or 10 cm in the menu). Perfect hits moves every hit to the sweet spot. Both are on by default, at 10 cm
Short swing assist
For drops, slow shots and short-swing volleys; on by default (Slow swings + timing), with a switch on the Racquet & settings tab. Slow swings: the hit assist also helps swings from about 2 km/h of racquet speed (instead of 7). Slow swings + timing: also, a hit is played at the top speed the strings reached within 35 ms before or after the ball met them, so a short swing no longer has to meet the ball at its very peak. A full swing is not changed
Tuning
The Ball physics tab adjusts 22 values (bounce, grip, shell lag, spin, air, strings) live, with rigid-ball and no-spin switches, a drop test, replays of your last hit and test shots in real time or slow motion
Nick
Emerges from the ball flattening into the wall–floor joint; targets are solved and verified with the same physics
Racquet
Open throat with bridge, 500 cm² head, 16×20 strings, 8×18 mm frame; 135 g, balance 353 mm, string-bed trampoline that settles between hits (a volley rally to yourself plays every hit off the same strings), frame mishits
Solver
Adaptive substeps, from 1 ms in flight down to 2 µs in hard impacts, swing interpolated between frames, speeding up through the frame as a real swing does: the same shot gives the same result at any refresh rate from 72 to 240 Hz

Runs at the highest refresh rate your headset offers and steps down by itself if it starts dropping frames: 120 Hz on Quest 2 and 3S, up to 207 Hz on Quest 3 (Horizon OS 2.7 or later, if the Browser offers it to web pages: the menu shows what it offers), or 207 / 240 Hz when forced in developer mode. Clear about 2 × 2 m of floor, or about 3 m across to walk back to the T between shots, and keep your guardian on: you will swing hard.
